sources.text:
Risovača Cave, (Serbian Cyrillic: Пећина Рисовача, romanized: Pećina Risovača) is situated at the very entrance of the town of Aranđelovac in central Serbia around 17 m (56 ft) above the Kubršnica river valley. It is one of the most important archaeological sites of the Paleolithic in Serbia besides the Gradac Cave near Kragujevac. Its discovery confirmed the assumed existence of the Paleolithic culture south of the Sava-Danube line and provided new information on the life of prehistoric humans in Europe.


== Geography ==
Formation of the Risovača cave started during the Cretaceous. It was created by the warm, mineral waters, which are abundant in the region surrounding Aranđelovac. The cave contains some natural rarities, like the marble onyx, which deposited from the water on the floor of the cave. It also contains aragonite, which groups its crystals on the ceiling of the cave (branching stalactite forms called flos-ferri ("flowers of iron"), seemingly defying the gravity.


== Discovery ==

Es ist eine der wichtigsten archäologischen Stätten des Paläolithikums in Serbien neben der Gradac-Höhle in der Nähe von Kragujevac.
